entry.author: Eastern Institute Of Technology
entry.summary:
From study to stronger community connections, Te Reo Māori is shaping careers at Gisborne District Council.

We’re proud to share this kōrero from Kelsey Goldsmith and Graeme Card, two EIT Te Reo Māori graduates who are now using their learning every day in their roles at Gisborne District Council.

As a policy planner, Kelsey explains how essential tikanga and te reo are in her mahi, guiding the way she engages with people and places across the region. Graeme, who works in an outward facing role with iwi and hapū, shares how learning te reo and understanding tikanga has deepened his ability to connect, communicate, and work respectfully with the community.
Both Kelsey and Graeme say their EIT courses have been invaluable in growing their confidence, their capability, and their careers.

If you’re working alongside iwi, hapū, or community groups, or want to strengthen your personal understanding of te ao Māori, take the next steps in your study journey with EIT Tairāwhiti, we’re local, like you.
